source.title: QUANDA.SKILLS — Creative Production, Aesthetic, Technique & Tutorial Retrieval Knowledge Base

metadata.Purpose: Agent-facing reference for interpreting creative intent, classifying references, mapping aesthetics to techniques and tools, decomposing projects into learnable skills, retrieving reliable tutorials, and adapting production roadmaps.
metadata.Scope note: Creative practice is open-ended, culturally vast, interdisciplinary, and continuously evolving. No finite document can literally contain every aesthetic, technique, tool, movement, cultural tradition, programming language, workflow, or future practice. This catalog is intentionally broad and retrieval-oriented: treat entries as canonical anchors, aliases, and expansion seeds rather than a closed universe.
metadata.Ontology note: Separate what a user WANTS (creative intent) from what a project REQUIRES (technical execution). An aesthetic tag should not automatically imply a specific technique, culture, software, or level of skill. Use relationships, confidence, and user confirmation.
metadata.Cultural note: Cultural, Indigenous, religious, regional, and historical labels are contextual descriptors, not interchangeable visual presets. Preserve provenance, avoid flattening living traditions into stereotypes, and prefer specific communities, periods, makers, techniques, and sources when known.
metadata.Retrieval note: Match tutorials primarily by required skill + technique + output + software/version + prerequisite level; use aesthetic similarity as a secondary reranking signal unless the tutorial specifically teaches that aesthetic treatment.
metadata.Conventions: Canonical labels are written in plain language. Slash-separated terms indicate close aliases or paired concepts. Parenthetical notes disambiguate use. Keep user-facing labels localizable; internal IDs should be stable, lowercase, ASCII-safe slugs.
